column5: Not a duplicate: stratospheric-thermal-structure mentions the ozone hole only for the vortex feedback (no CFC chemistry, Chapman, Montreal Protocol). Chapman 1930, Molina-Rowland 1974, Farman et al. 1985, ~1e5 O3 per Cl, Antarctic return to 1980 levels ~2066 (2023 assessment): en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ozone_depletion. 220 DU hole threshold: NASA Ozone Watch (svs.gsfc.nasa.gov). Universal ratification 16 Sep 2009: Wikipedia Montreal Protocol and the UNEP ozone archive. 1995 Nobel Chemistry (Crutzen, Molina, Rowland), ~90% of ozone in stratosphere, PSC conversion of HCl/ClONO2 to Cl2, ~100 km turbopause: standard (WMO Ozone Q&A). Stratospheric chlorine decline since late 1990s is consistent (EESC peaked late 1990s; tropospheric EECl 1994). Hard prereq formal-systems = stage; ok.

Not a duplicate (photochemical smog mentioned once, in atmospheric-inversion-temperature). Haagen-Smit: ozone in LA smog 1948, NOx + hydrocarbons + sunlight mechanism published 1950-52 (Ind. Eng. Chem. 1952), so "early 1950s" holds: PBS "Mystery of LA's smog revealed", NASA in-the-fog-about-smog.pdf. Six NAAQS criteria pollutants, PM2.5, Great Smog Dec 1952 (thousands of deaths, 4,000-12,000 estimates), NO2 photolysis / NO titration / peroxy-radical NO->NO2, PAN, NO->NO2->O3 diurnal order, subsidence inversion under highs: standard (Seinfeld & Pandis ch. 6; EPA NAAQS). Hard prereq formal-systems; ok.

Not a duplicate (NWP named only in passing in remote-sensing-atmosphere, explosive-cyclogenesis-bombogenesis; weather-forecasting-basics is K-5). Richardson 1922, >=6 weeks of hand work for a 6 h forecast, 145 hPa/6 h error from unbalanced initial data; Charney-Fjortoft-von Neumann 1950 ENIAC barotropic vorticity (500 hPa) forecast: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_numerical_weather_prediction, Lynch NWP50 (atmos.uw.edu/~dargan/542/Lynch_NWP50.pdf). Lorenz 1963 convection model, ~2-week predictability, Bjerknes 1904 programme, NWS PoP = probability of >=0.01 in at a point, parameterization of sub-grid convection: standard (Kalnay 2003; NWS PoP definition). Hard prereq formal-systems; ok.

Not a duplicate: physics dispersion-and-prisms / wavelength-color-refractive-index mention rainbows as dispersion examples; no topic covers halos, sun dogs, coronas, mirages. Overlaps the sky-color part of the new physics rayleigh-scattering (same batch); orchestrator may add a soft edge. Primary 42 deg / secondary 51 deg reversed, Alexander's dark band, 22 deg halo from 60 deg ice prism (min deviation 21.8 deg recomputed with n=1.31), sun dogs from horizontal plates ~22 deg at Sun's elevation, coronas by droplet diffraction: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halo_(optical_phenomenon), rmets.org haloes-and-sun-dogs, itlab.us Atmospheric_Optics.pdf. Red outermost (smallest deviation), no primary bow for Sun > 42 deg, 1/lambda^4, inferior/superior mirage ray bending: standard (Ahrens ch. 19). Hard prereq dispersion-and-prisms stage <= formal-systems; ok.

Not a duplicate, but partial overlap: social-sciences/human-geography/climate-adaptation-communities covers adaptation equity and justice only (no mitigation, TCRE, carbon budgets, CDR); orchestrator may add a soft edge. SR1.5: ~45% below 2010 by 2030, net zero ~2050 for no/limited overshoot: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_Report_on_Global_Warming_of_1.5C, downtoearth.org.in SR1.5 coverage. Paris 2015 "well below 2 C ... pursue 1.5 C" and NDCs (UNFCCC Art. 2, 4); near-linear TCRE and near-zero committed warming after net zero (AR6 WG1 SPM D.1); methane lifetime ~12 yr (AR6 11.8 yr). Hard prereq climate-change-science is advanced = stage; ok.

Not a duplicate: solar-variability-climate uses sunspots/Maunder for climate forcing; radiation-belt-dynamics mentions CMEs; the-sun is K-5. Sunspots ~3800-4200 K vs ~5800 K photosphere, rotation ~25 d equator vs ~36 d near poles ("about 35" is an acceptable round figure): pressbooks Fanshawe astronomy 10.4, windows2universe differential_rotation, cesar.esa.int guide. Core 15 MK, age 4.6 Gyr, radiative zone to ~0.7 R, granules ~1000 km, corona > 1 MK, solar wind 300-800 km/s, 11-yr cycle / 22-yr Hale cycle, Maunder Minimum 1645-1715, radiative diffusion 1e4-1.7e5 yr (Mitalas & Sills 1992), 8.3 min light time, CME 1-3 day transit, Carrington 1859, Hydro-Quebec 13 Mar 1989: standard (OpenStax Astronomy 2e ch. 15-16). Hard prereq electromagnetic-spectrum-astronomy formal-systems = stage; soft prereqs at advanced are allowed; ok.

Not a duplicate (GOE/BIF only in passing in redox-geochemistry, organic-geochemistry, atmospheric-chemistry-planets, two microbiology files). GOE ~2.4 Ga marked by S-MIF loss (2.50-2.43 Ga, PNAS 2020 pmc PMC7306805; MIF persisting to ~2.31 Ga, Nat. Commun. 2018 PMC5993798), consistent with "about 2.4" and red beds "after ~2.3 Ga". Earth 4.54 Ga, Jack Hills zircons 4.4 Ga with 18O evidence for water (Wilde et al. 2001 Nature), faint young Sun ~70% (Gough 1981), stromatolites ~3.48 Ga (Dresser Fm.), BIF mostly > 1.8 Ga, detrital pyrite/uraninite loss, Neoproterozoic oxygenation 800-540 Ma, cyanobacteria as first oxygenic phototrophs and chloroplast origin: standard (Holland 2006 Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B; Lyons et al. 2014 Nature). Hard prereq geological-time-scale formal-systems = stage; ok.

Not a duplicate (ore/placer/porphyry only in passing in geophysics exploration files, recycling-and-sustainability, sediment-provenance-detrital-minerals). Cu in continental crust 27-75 ppm across estimates, all < 0.01% (earthref.org GERMRD e:29; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abundance_of_elements_in_Earth's_crust). Bushveld chromitite/PGM layers, Andean porphyry Cu over subduction, BIF as main iron ore, evaporites, placer Au/diamond/cassiterite, residual bauxite, aggregates largest by volume, AMD from pyrite oxidation, reserve vs resource as economic terms (USGS Circular 831): standard (Tarbuck ch. 21; Robb, Introduction to Ore-Forming Processes). Hard prereq rock-forming-minerals formal-systems = stage; ok.

Not a duplicate (firn/accumulation only in ice-core-paleoclimate-analysis; erosion-by-wind-and-ice covers landforms, not formation/flow/mass balance). Q2 answer said firn becomes ice "after years to centuries"; cold polar sites take up to ~2,500 yr (Vostok; Byrd ~280 yr): antarcticglaciers.org "From Snow to Firn to Glacier ice"; Cambridge J. Glaciol. firn review. Changed to "years to thousands of years depending on temperature and snowfall". Antarctica+Greenland ~99% of glacier ice, ice ~10% of land, brittle zone ~50 m, Agassiz 1837 (Neuchatel address), LGM ~20 ka with sea level ~120 m lower, Fennoscandia/Hudson Bay GIA, till vs outwash, equatorial glaciers (Kilimanjaro, Andes): standard (Tarbuck ch. 18; Cuffey & Paterson). No hard prereqs; formal-systems fits; ok.

Not a duplicate ("geosphere" appears elsewhere only in nutrient-cycling-phosphorus-sulfur; no earth-systems topic). Explainer defined "feedback" as "a change that strengthens itself", which is only a positive feedback; reworded to define feedback as a loop, call ice-albedo a positive feedback, and note that others weaken a change (standard; NGSS MS-ESS2/HS-ESS2-2 language). 97% ocean, ~69% of fresh water in ice, ~30% groundwater, ~1% surface: usgs.gov/water-science-school/science/where-earths-water. Volcanic sulfate cooling 1-2 yr (Pinatubo), photosynthesis changing the atmosphere, cryosphere naming, Sun vs internal heat as energy sources: standard. No hard prereqs; concrete-operations fits NGSS 5-ESS2-1; ok.

Not a duplicate (mathematics contour-maps / contour-maps-level-curves are multivariable functions; geomorphology, lidar, photogrammetry mention topo maps in passing). Index contours every fifth line (every 4th or 5th by interval) and hachured depression contours: usgs.gov US Topo Cartographic Specifications - Elevation. V upstream rule, no-crossing / overhang exception, spacing = steepness, profiles: standard (USGS Topographic Map Symbols booklet; NY Regents ESRT). Recomputed Q2 80 m / 2 km = 40 m/km, 1:24,000 -> 240 m per cm, 200/4 = 50 m/km. No hard prereqs; abstract-reasoning fits middle-school map skills; ok.

Not a duplicate (pseudorange/RTK/trilateration appear only in passing in photogrammetry and seismology files; gps-geodesy-and-crustal-deformation applies GPS to tectonics). >=24-slot constellation, six planes, ~20,200 km MEO, two orbits per day (11 h 58 m): gps.gov/systems/gps/space, gssc.esa.int Navipedia GPS Space Segment. Recomputed 1 us x c = 300 m. Four unknowns (x,y,z,clock bias), receive-only receivers, WGS 84, relativistic clock offset (~38 us/day; Ashby 2003 Living Rev. Relativ.), ionospheric/tropospheric delay, multipath, DOP, DGNSS base-station corrections, RTK carrier phase cm-level, consumer few-m accuracy: standard (Bolstad GIS Fundamentals ch. 5; Misra & Enge). Hard prereq coordinate-systems-projections advanced = stage; ok.

Not a duplicate (well logs only as inputs in gravity-surveys, seismic-interpretation, synthetic-seismogram-modeling, vp-vs-ratio). First electrical log 5 Sep 1927, Pechelbronn, Alsace, team led by Henri Doll for the Schlumberger brothers: slb.com/who-we-are/our-history/1920s, en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Well_logging. Archie 1942 (Shell), first quantitative saturation relation: Wikipedia Well logging, spec2000.net Crain-Ganz history. Recomputed Q2 phi = 0.33/1.65 = 0.20 and Q3 Sw^2 = 0.05/(0.04 x 10) = 0.125, Sw = 0.354. GR from K-40/U/Th in clays, Compton-scattering density tool, neutron hydrogen index, gas crossover, sonic slower in porous rock, impedance = rho x V for synthetics: standard (Kearey, Brooks & Hill ch. 11; Ellis & Singer). Hard prereq sedimentary-rocks formal-systems < advanced; ok.

Not a duplicate (microplastics/oil spills appear elsewhere only in microbial-biotechnology-industrial-applications; biomagnification overlaps biology bioaccumulation-and-ecological-toxicology, which is linked as a prereq). Jambeck et al. 2015 Science: 4.8-12.7 Mt from land in 2010: jambeck.engr.uga.edu/landplasticinput. <5 mm microplastic definition (NOAA workshop, Arthur et al. 2009), Ekman convergence in subtropical gyres, GPGP between Hawaii and California, Minamata methylmercury 1950s, Exxon Valdez 1989, Deepwater Horizon 2010, seeps + chronic sources > large spills (NRC Oil in the Sea), land-based sources dominant, oiled-feather hypothermia: standard (Garrison Oceanography ch. 18). No hard prereqs; formal-systems fits APES; ok. Style only (not a factual error): reworded the Explainer's "is not a solid island. It is a broad area" (banned not-X-it's-Y form).

Not a duplicate (passing mentions in everyday-acids-and-bases, chemical-weathering, biology files). Explainer said Robert Angus Smith coined "acid rain" in 1872; sources put first use at 1852 or 1859, with 1872 the book Air and Rain (chemistryworld.com Reed biography review; undiscoveredscotland.co.uk; shapero.com listing). Reworded to "introduced the term in the mid-1800s ... 1872 book Air and Rain". Recomputed 10^1 and 10^1.4 = 25. pH 5.6 from CO2, 1990 CAAA Title IV SO2 cap-and-trade, aluminum mobilization, Ca/Mg leaching, Adirondacks/Scandinavia granitic sensitivity, tall stacks UK->Scandinavia, pH low-4s in 1970s-80s E. US: standard (EPA Acid Rain Program; Likens et al.). Hard prereq formal-systems; ok.
